title: Appearances can be deceptive
caption: The open cluster NGC 411, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 411 · constellation Tucana · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: At first glance NGC 411 looks like a typical globular cluster, a crowd of stars of many colors and brightnesses. Appearances can deceive. It is not a globular cluster, its stars are not old, and it does not even belong to the Milky Way.

NGC 411 is classed as an open cluster. Such clusters are less tightly bound than globulars, and their stars drift apart over time, while globulars have endured for well over 10 billion years. NGC 411 is not much more than a tenth of that age, and its stars are only a fraction of the Sun's age.

All its stars formed at roughly the same time from a single cloud of gas, yet they come in different sizes. The range of colors and brightnesses in Hubble's view tells astronomers about each star's mass, temperature and stage of life. Blue stars, for example, have hotter surfaces than red ones.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.42 x 1.82 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 141 × 106 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This composite combines ultraviolet, visible and infrared observations from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, reaching a little beyond both the violet and red ends of the spectrum. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet and infrared light in this image lie just beyond what the human eye can detect.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Around 150 globular clusters are scattered around our galaxy, and Hubble's sharp resolution picks out single stars even in their packed centers. NGC 411 lies about 200,000 light-years away.
alt: A cluster of stars showing a wide range of colors and brightnesses.
